predecessors.name: Ottoman Empire
predecessors.text: Tiberias, taken by Daher al-Umar in 1730 with Saqr Bedouin support; Galilee, under Ottoman rule

successors.name: Ottoman Empire
successors.text: Acre transferred by Hasan Pasha to Ahmad al-Jazzar on 19 September 1775; Galilee after Deir Hanna fell in 1776; part of Sidon Eyalet, with Acre as Jazzar's seat

ledger.x: c. 1740: Safed and Nazareth. He took Safed c. 1740 and 'Nazareth came under his control by the end of 1740'.
1744: Acre. He 'took Acre by force, probably in this year', and was formally appointed its multazim in July 1746.
c. 1750: the headquarters move from Deir Hanna to Acre (Deir Hanna was his sons' and brother Sa'd's fortified base).
1775: Daher's death ends the Metawali alliance.
May 1775: Gaza, Ramla and Jaffa fall to Egypt.
12 June 1775: the Egyptian invasion ends with Abu al-Dhahab's death on 10 June; Gaza, Ramla and Jaffa stay lost.
7 August 1775: Hasan Pasha's flotilla arrives at Haifa and then Acre, bombarding it.

wars.name: Ottoman campaigns against Daher al-Umar (1738-1743)
wars.outcome: Sulayman Pasha al-Azm's abortive attack (1738); Ibrahim Pasha of Sidon beaten near Acre (1741); the 90-day siege of Tiberias (September 1742-1743), Sulayman dying in August 1743.

wars.name: Daher and Ali Bey against Damascus (1770-1773)
wars.outcome: Ali Bey's campaign began in November 1770; Daher cleared Gaza and Ramla, took Jaffa (August 1771) and Sidon (June 1771); Abu al-Dhahab went over to the Ottomans in 1772; Daher retook Jaffa on 16 February 1773; Ali Bey died in 1773.

wars.name: Abu al-Dhahab's Palestine campaign
wars.outcome: May 1775: Gaza, Ramla, Jaffa taken; Acre surrendered 30 May; Abu al-Dhahab died on 10 June; Daher re-entered Acre on 12 June.

wars.name: Hasan Pasha's campaign against Acre
wars.outcome: Hasan Pasha's flotilla reached Haifa on 7 August 1775 and bombarded Acre; Daher was killed on 22 August; Acre went to Jazzar on 19 September; Ali held Galilee until Deir Hanna fell in June or on 22 July 1776.

certainty.note: Tax-farm (iltizam) territories held by a sheikh, drawn as radii around towns; no boundary is described.
